title: Error 3x7E - Optimizer Mismatch
shortDescription: Optimizer count does not match pairing list.
fullDescription:
After commissioning, the SolarEdge inverter knows how many optimizers should report. If one fails, is not paired, or an extra is added, Error 3x7E appears.

Installers must re-pair or remove the optimizer in SetApp/Monitoring.

fixSteps.title: Installer re-pair
fixSteps.instruction: Use SetApp > Pair to re-run pairing.

faq.a: No, the inverter is locked until pairing completes.

title: Error 5 - String Fault
shortDescription: DC string voltage outside expected range.
fullDescription:
Error 5 indicates the series string voltage is wrong - usually a disconnected optimizer output, polarity swap, or damaged cable.

DC strings are live during daylight; only installers should troubleshoot.

fixSteps.title: Installer diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: DC string voltage test at inverter.

faq.a: Yes, chewed DC cables are a real cause.

title: Error 7 - Arc Fault Detected
shortDescription: AFCI detected DC arc on string.
fullDescription:
Per UL 1699B, SolarEdge inverters must shut down on detected arcs. Loose MC4 connectors are the usual culprit; genuine arcs can ignite the roof.

Have an installer inspect immediately before reclosing.

fixSteps.title: Call installer
fixSteps.instruction: Do not manually reset - inspect first.

faq.a: No, that defeats the safety system.

title: Error 8 - AC Over Voltage
fullDescription:
Error 8 is triggered when the service voltage rises too high, often worse when the inverter itself injects power.

Utility tap adjustment or inverter volt-watt curve tuning usually resolves it.

causes.cause: Long AC run causing voltage rise

faq.q: Is this my problem or the utility?
faq.a: Usually the utility; installer can prove it with logs.

title: Error 10 - DC Isolation Fault
shortDescription: Insulation resistance between DC and ground too low.
fullDescription:
An insulation test at inverter startup reveals a leakage path to ground - often caused by wet connections, damaged cable jacket, or water in a j-box.

This blocks startup and requires installer diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Installer isolation test
fixSteps.instruction: Insulation resistance test on each string.

faq.a: Water-induced leakage evaporates as panels warm up.

title: Error 61 - AC Under Frequency
fullDescription:
Utility frequency dipped below the anti-islanding threshold. Usually transient and clears automatically.

Persistent trips may indicate generator-supplied power.

faq.q: Do I need to do anything?

title: Error 18 - RCD Trip
fullDescription:
Internal RCD detected leakage current exceeding 30 mA. Could be nuisance from damp conditions or a real fault.

Installer inspection is required.

title: Error 119 - Internal Software Fault
fullDescription:
Firmware reported a NaN (not-a-number) in a calculation - usually an early-firmware bug. A firmware update typically fixes it.

Contact SolarEdge support via installer.

faq.a: Temporarily; firmware update is the real fix.

title: Error 156 - Pairing Failure
shortDescription: Inverter could not complete optimizer pairing.
fullDescription:
Pairing cycles through optimizers on the string. If a unit fails to respond within the timeout, pairing stops and error 156 is reported. Usually one faulty optimizer or DC wiring issue.

Installer troubleshoots.

faq.q: Can I skip the bad optimizer?
faq.a: No, each must pair for proper string voltage.

title: Modbus Communication Error
fullDescription:
SolarEdge uses Modbus RS-485 for the revenue meter and some battery/EV chargers. Wiring, termination, and unique address settings all affect reliability.

Installer inspects wiring and settings.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Installer confirms A/B pairs and termination.

faq.a: Only for some accessories; meter remains Modbus.

title: Battery Off-Line
shortDescription: Storage battery is isolated from the inverter.
fullDescription:
The battery may be off-line due to disabled backup mode, low SOC cutoff, or a disconnect breaker. Normal for deep-discharge protection.

Check SOC and backup reserve settings in the monitoring app.

fixSteps.title: Allow recharge
fixSteps.instruction: Let battery charge above low SOC cutoff via solar or grid.

repairTime: Up to several hours for SOC recovery

faq.a: Yes, when SOC rises above the cutoff.

title: Rapid Shutdown Engaged
shortDescription: Array reduced to safe voltage per NEC 690.12.
fullDescription:
Triggered by pressing the RSD button or de-energizing the AC circuit. Panel voltages drop below 30 V within 30 seconds.

Reset by restoring AC and toggling the RSD switch.

fixSteps.title: Restore AC
fixSteps.instruction: Close AC breaker and RSD switch.

faq.a: Yes, under NEC 690.12 for roof arrays.

title: String Voltage Too Low
shortDescription: Series string not reaching minimum start voltage.
fullDescription:
SolarEdge strings must meet a minimum DC voltage for the inverter to track. A fallen optimizer, missing panel, or mispairing keeps the string short.

Review string design and count via installer.

fixSteps.title: Installer check
fixSteps.instruction: Verify optimizer pairing and string length.

faq.q: Can I add a panel to help?
faq.a: Only under design review; exceeding limits voids warranty.

title: Inverter Overheating
fullDescription:
Inverters derate above ~60 C heat sink temperature. Sun-exposed mount, clogged vents, or failing fan are common causes.

Relocating the inverter or adding a sunshade helps.

fixSteps.title: Clean exterior
fixSteps.instruction: Gently clean vents with compressed air (power OFF).

fixSteps.title: Add sunshade
fixSteps.instruction: Installer fits a sunshade per SolarEdge guide.

faq.a: It protects it; losing production is the cost.

title: Firmware Update Pending or Failed
shortDescription: Firmware download or flash did not complete.
fullDescription:
Updates require inverter online via Wi-Fi/Ethernet/Cell. Weak connection can stall the update.

Installer can force update via SetApp over Bluetooth locally.

fixSteps.title: SetApp local update
fixSteps.instruction: Installer connects via SetApp and pushes firmware.
